core_obligations: Right exactness (proof lines 3029-3030): the functor on sheaves is a left adjoint, hence right exact.

Left exactness (proof lines 3031-3040): it suffices to show commutation with finite limits; the auxiliary indexing categories are filtered, so the left Kan extension commutes with finite limits by the general commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits, and sheafification commutes with finite limits as well, which gives the claim since the functor on sheaves is the composite of the two.
proof_roadmap: Use the adjunction for right exactness.
Use filteredness of the auxiliary categories to get commutation with finite limits for the functor on presheaves.
Compose with sheafification, which is exact for finite limits, to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a continuous functor whose auxiliary categories are filtered defines a morphism of sites, that is, the induced functor on sheaves is exact (statement lines 3018-3026). The proof is a complete argument: right exactness holds because the functor is a left adjoint (proof lines 3029-3030); it remains to prove commutation with finite limits, which follows from filteredness of the auxiliary categories together with the commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits (proof lines 3031-3037); and composing with sheafification, which commutes with finite limits, gives the claim (proof lines 3038-3040). The non-formal content is the reduction to the presheaf level. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
